name: ta-weight-085-signal-amplitude
rationale: Measured on the current code, not guessed. Simulator::run calls `TradingEngine::compute_btc_target(point, &[], &trading_config)` with an EMPTY news slice (src/backtest/simulator.rs:127), so in every backtest this pipeline has ever run avg_sentiment is exactly 0.0 and sentiment_normalized is pinned at exactly 0.5. The composite is therefore `combined = 0.7 * ta_normalized + 0.3 * 0.5 = 0.7 * ta + 0.15`, which spans [0.15, 0.85] no matter what the indicators do. With experiments/baseline-config.json's zone (hold_jpy_below 0.1, hold_btc_above 0.9, range_max 1.0) apply_zone's saturation arms trigger at raw < 0.1 and raw > 0.9, so BOTH are structurally unreachable: the allocation target is confined to [0.0625, 0.9375] and the strategy can never go fully to JPY or fully to BTC, however saturated every indicator is. That also means 30% of the signal's dynamic range is spent on a constant, damping the amplitude of every allocation swing by the same 30%. This hypothesis moves ta_weight 0.70 -> 0.85 and sentiment_weight 0.30 -> 0.15, the single smallest change that tests whether restoring amplitude helps, leaving every indicator period, the threshold and the zone byte-identical to the baseline. It is not full-ta-weight-no-sentiment (rejected 2026-09-08 at ta 1.0 / sentiment 0.0): that variant removed news entirely and, decisively, was measured on the CoinGecko 1-hour series that docs/self-improvement-loop.md's 'Data source' section says is not comparable to the current bitFlyer 1-minute bars -- its -0.67% is not evidence about today's setup. Keeping sentiment_weight at 0.15 rather than 0.0 also keeps news a live input on the running instance, where the cache is NOT empty, so a promotion here would not silently delete a production signal.
